entries.title: A Quick search box in the bottom bar
entries.body: On your own articles, the bar along the bottom of the page has a Quick search box: type, pause, and Search opens with the passages that match. Press / to jump to it, Enter to search at once, Escape to clear it; on a touch screen, in a narrow window or when space runs short it is a lightning-bolt button instead. Separately, quick search in the Search panel runs whenever you pause after three or more characters, keeping one saved search per burst of typing rather than one per pause.

entries.title: Remember gains a Tutorial; Recall adapts to you
entries.body: Remember has three parts: Recall, Tutorial and Quiz. Tutorial is new: it aims to teach a little of the article each turn, set you one task (say it back, apply it, or push back), and return to earlier points every three or four turns. Recall drops its four reply styles for one approach that aims to keep replies short, answer direct questions, and fill in a gap when you are stuck rather than make you fail twice.

entries.title: Bookmarks stand out, and comments need no AI
entries.body: A bookmarked paragraph gets a filled, full-strength mark beside it, and bookmarking opens a comment box unless you have moved on; closing it keeps the bookmark. The box says the AI does not reply, so a comment can be just yours. Comments are labelled Bookmark, Comment, Comment + AI or Question, and your passage questions appear in the margin notes.

entries.title: Quotes mark the strip; headings stay in view
entries.body: The lines Quotes picks out show as green marks on the strip showing where you are in the article, in every mode. Point at one in the text for its card, with previous and next; Quotes mode adds large step buttons and arrow keys. With Experimental features on, the headings you are under stay at the top as you read.

entries.title: Easier tapping on library cards and close crosses
entries.body: Library cards keep their actions on the bottom row; on a touch screen, wide cards show large action icons instead of a menu, and narrow ones a clearer menu button. The close crosses on dialogs and panels now share one size, with a bigger tap area on touch screens. The panel's scrollbar is easier to see, where the browser allows.

entries.title: Brief summaries aim for plainer words
entries.body: New Brief summaries are told to use everyday words even if your profile says expert: at most two technical terms, each explained. Every level aims to start with what the piece is after and what kind of piece it is. Older summaries are marked out of date, not redone. A cancelled drag on the level slider still asks for the new level.

entries.title: Citations sort by date; Debate seeks citing work
entries.body: Citations can be ordered by date: oldest first, by the year each work shows, undated works last, offered when at least one work has a year. New Debate searches ask for work that cites and discusses the article, scholarly work included, and check more than the first passage they find on a page.

entries.title: Feedback you send is also emailed to us
entries.body: When you send feedback, a plain-text copy may also be emailed to our own inbox, with what you wrote, the page address and your email address. The privacy policy says so. Sending the same report twice does not send a second email.
